title: Is ChatGPT A Good Translator? Yes With GPT-4 As The Engine
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether ChatGPT can function as a machine translation system and how its performance compares with commercial translation products. The authors focus on three questions: how to prompt ChatGPT for translation, how it performs across language pairs with different resource levels and language families, and how robust it is on domain-specific or noisy text.

The approach is an empirical benchmark evaluation rather than an educational intervention. The study tests several translation prompts on ChatGPT, compares ChatGPT against Google Translate, DeepL, and Tencent TranSmart, and evaluates translation quality using BLEU, ChrF++, and TER. It examines multiple language directions involving German, English, Romanian, and Chinese, plus robustness sets from biomedical abstracts, Reddit comments, and speech-like data. The authors also test a pivot prompting strategy and later re-evaluate performance with GPT-4 as the engine.

The paper finds that ChatGPT with GPT-3.5 performs reasonably well on high-resource European language pairs but lags on low-resource and distant language pairs, and it is less robust than commercial systems on biomedical and noisy text. Pivot prompting improves performance for distant languages, and GPT-4 substantially improves translation quality to near-commercial levels. The authors conclude that ChatGPT becomes a strong translator with GPT-4, though the work is limited by small samples and early-access constraints.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed technical report on machine translation, not an education study, and it does not evaluate any K-12 learning intervention or student outcome. It provides benchmark-based comparisons of translation systems rather than empirical evidence about educational achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct impact on middle school mathematics achievement or any education outcome. The paper's findings concern translation quality for GPT-3.5/GPT-4 versus commercial MT systems, which is outside the retrieved research topic.
